calls.head: Don’t judge the Maple Leafs by last season
calls.body: Over this season and last, the Maple Leafs have been near the bottom of the league for shot volume. This season alone they’ve been around the middle of the league, shooting more. We think tonight looks more like this season than the old Maple Leafs.
calls.call: The Maple Leafs’ shot volume is better than their blended level of 54.1 per 60.
calls.nums: Shot volume: 24th over two seasons (54.1 per 60), 14th this season (56.8 per 60)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · blended and this season only · 4 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60, Toronto had 56.6 per 60, against 54.1 per 60 over this season and last and 56.8 per 60 this season alone.

calls.head: Bobrovsky’s record against the Golden Knights is a coincidence
calls.body: Bobrovsky has been a wall against the Golden Knights since 2023-24, well above his usual. It looks like a pattern, but across three seasons a goalie’s record against one team told us nothing about the next meeting. Expect the usual Bobrovsky.
calls.call: If Bobrovsky starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .901 than to his .935 against the Golden Knights.
calls.nums: 6 starts against Vegas: .935 save percentage · .901 against everyone else
calls.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 6 against Vegas, 4,098 shots against everyone else
calls.happened: S. Bobrovsky stopped 40 of 43 shots (.930), against his usual .901 and his .935 against this team before tonight.

calls.head: The Golden Knights’ power play has a target
calls.body: The Golden Knights’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Maple Leafs’ kill is one of the league’s worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Maple Leafs more than most.
calls.call: The Golden Knights’ power play creates at least their usual 9.0 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: Vegas 2nd for power play (9.0 expected goals per 60) · Toronto 31st for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 4 games this season
calls.happened: Vegas’s power play created 9.8 expected goals per 60 in 8:00 of 5-on-4 time, against their usual 9.0, and scored 0 goals.

calls.head: Quality over quantity for the Golden Knights
calls.body: The Golden Knights make their shots count, and the Maple Leafs are around the middle of the league at preventing dangerous shots. Expect the Golden Knights to get some real chances.
calls.call: The Golden Knights’ average shot has at least their usual 6.7% chance of going in.
calls.nums: Vegas 7th for shot quality (a 6.7% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Toronto 22nd for preventing dangerous shots
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 4 games this season
calls.happened: Vegas’s average shot had a 5.5% chance of going in, against their usual 6.7%.

VGK.head: We gave Vegas a 80% chance, and Vegas delivered.

TOR.head: We gave Toronto only a 20% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Toronto hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Toronto’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 41, against their usual 90 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: A big night for S. Bobrovsky
surprises.body: S. Bobrovsky allowed 3 goals on shots worth 5.1 expected goals, 2.1 fewer than expected. Starting goalies had a night this good about once every 15 starts over the last three seasons.

story.head: The Golden Knights come back from three down
paras: Jack Roslovic opened the scoring 34 seconds in. The Maple Leafs led 3-0 before the first period was half over. The Golden Knights came all the way back, and won it in the shootout.
The score was fair. Replay this game’s chances a hundred times and the Golden Knights win nine in ten.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Golden Knights.
Jack Eichel has a point in every game this season.
Nick Paul scored his first goal of the season.
Two of the preview’s four calls held.
